answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a crystal deposit held in escrow. Creating thousands of clones then costs real capital, not just a new name. The stake grows with reputation earned over time, similar to tending an orchard rather than crossing a canyon in one leap: newcomers start with small limits and only gain larger trading rights after a history of honest, verifiable work. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its history burned, so a Sybil attacker must pay again for every fake copy.
